items.question: At 12 weeks, what mean orientation score did the authors report, and was that number author-reported or calculated from the excerpt?
items.direct_answer: The authors reported a 12-week mean orientation score of 82.4 points; the value was author-reported, not calculated from the excerpt (n=36).
items.checked_scope: Checked S1 (Twelve-week results) in full for the time point, mean orientation score, units, sample size, and reported-versus-derived provenance.

adversarial_review.omission: Both requested components are present: the 12-week orientation mean (82.4 points) and its author-reported rather than calculated provenance.
adversarial_review.comparator: Q1 requests one reported mean, not a group contrast; no between-group direction or baseline was invented.
adversarial_review.negation: The phrase 'not calculated from the excerpt' preserves the provenance limit while leaving the reported value intact.
adversarial_review.condition: The 12-week endpoint, orientation-score endpoint, points unit, and n=36 denominator all match S1.
adversarial_review.unsupported_generalization: The answer reports a study mean only; it makes no efficacy, participant-wide, or beyond-excerpt claim.
adversarial_review.whole_answer_entailment: The single S1 quotation contains the mean, time point, unit, sample size, and author-reported wording used by the answer; human entailment review remains required.
adversarial_review.conflicts_two_sided: No competing orientation mean appears in S1, S2, or T1, so there is no Q1 value conflict to reconcile.
adversarial_review.formula_derived_vs_author_reported: The 82.4-point value is labelled author-reported; SEM 1.2 was not used to derive a new estimate.
adversarial_review.status_integrity: Q1 is answered with one S1 evidence item whose anchor is inside its declared checked scope.

items.residual_uncertainty: No additional uncertainty is inferred beyond the excerpt's reported mean and SEM.

items.question: In Table 1 at the Reed site, how did Compass A's mean completion time compare with Compass B's, including the exploratory/unadjusted conditions and units, and can the comparison be generalized to other sites?
items.direct_answer: At the Reed site only, Compass A's mean completion time was 1.3 minutes lower than Compass B's (8.1 vs 9.4 minutes), a difference calculated from the two reported means; the comparison was exploratory and unadjusted (n=12 per group). No, this table does not support generalizing the comparison to other sites.
items.checked_scope: Checked T1 (Table 1, Reed-site exploratory completion times) in full for both means, units, comparator direction, sample size, conditions, and other-site scope.

adversarial_review.omission: The response supplies both Reed means, their direction and difference, minutes, per-group n, exploratory/unadjusted conditions, and an explicit answer about other-site generalization.
adversarial_review.comparator: Compass A (8.1 minutes) is correctly described as 1.3 minutes lower than Compass B (9.4 minutes), using B as the stated baseline.
adversarial_review.negation: The explicit 'No' blocks the requested other-site generalization instead of implying it from a favourable numerical difference.
adversarial_review.condition: Every comparison clause remains tied to Reed site only and to the exploratory, unadjusted T1 analysis with n=12 per group.
adversarial_review.unsupported_generalization: The response does not infer superiority at other sites or statistical significance from an unadjusted descriptive comparison.
adversarial_review.whole_answer_entailment: T1 supports both input means and all restrictions; the matrix separately documents the calculated subtraction rather than pretending T1 reports 1.3 minutes.
adversarial_review.conflicts_two_sided: T1 contains one Reed comparison and no other-site completion results, so the answer does not suppress a competing site estimate.

formula_derived_vs_author_reported.formula: 9.4 minutes - 8.1 minutes = 1.3 minutes; Compass A minus Compass B = -1.3 minutes, so A is 1.3 minutes lower.
inputs: Compass A: author-reported 8.1 minutes at Reed
Compass B: author-reported 9.4 minutes at Reed
formula_derived_vs_author_reported.rounding: One decimal place, matching both reported inputs; the difference is calculated, not author-reported.

adversarial_review.status_integrity: Q2 is answered with mixed evidence: T1 supplies the reported means while the matrix records the derived direction and difference.

items.residual_uncertainty: The difference is exploratory, unadjusted, and restricted to Reed; no other-site or significance conclusion is supported.

items.question: What 95% confidence interval is reported for the 12-week mean orientation score?
items.direct_answer: Not reported in the checked excerpt: S1 gives the mean and SEM, but no reported 95% confidence interval or CI bounds for the 12-week mean orientation score; no CI was calculated.
items.checked_scope: Checked S1 (Twelve-week results), S2 (Statistical reporting), and T1 (Table 1) in full for a reported 95% confidence interval or lower/upper CI bounds. None appears. The SEM 1.2 in S1 is not treated as a CI; this not_reported status is limited to the supplied excerpt.

adversarial_review.omission: The response states that no 95% CI or CI bounds are reported for the 12-week mean and separately notes that no CI was calculated.
adversarial_review.comparator: Q3 requests interval bounds rather than an arm comparison; no lower/upper pair or arm contrast was fabricated.
adversarial_review.negation: 'Not reported in the checked excerpt' is explicitly bounded and does not become a claim that no study anywhere reports this interval.
adversarial_review.condition: The absence statement remains restricted to the 12-week orientation score and the enumerated S1, S2, and T1 excerpt anchors.
adversarial_review.unsupported_generalization: The answer neither converts SEM 1.2 into a confidence level nor invents a symmetric interval around 82.4 points.
adversarial_review.whole_answer_entailment: S1 provides the near-miss SEM while S2 explicitly excludes CI bounds and calculations; these are reviewed as scope evidence, not inserted as fake support quotes.
adversarial_review.conflicts_two_sided: The excerpt contains no competing CI bounds; the only potential confusion is SEM versus CI, which the answer resolves without substitution.
adversarial_review.formula_derived_vs_author_reported: No CI formula was applied and no interval is represented as author-reported; the task prohibits deriving one from SEM here.
adversarial_review.status_integrity: Q3 uses not_reported, retains evidence=[], and documents all three checked anchors rather than manufacturing an absence quotation.

items.residual_uncertainty: Not reported only in S1, S2, and T1 of the supplied excerpt; this is not a claim about other documents.
